title: Senator Imelda Sanmiguel Sánchez Confirms Interest in Running for Mayor of Nuevo Laredo in 2027
excerpt: PAN Senator Imelda Sanmiguel Sánchez of Tamaulipas has confirmed she wants to run for mayor of Nuevo Laredo in 2027 if her party selects her, and an October Electoralia poll places her at 22% among PAN profiles for the nomination.
content:
NUEVO LAREDO, Tamaulipas — Imelda Sanmiguel Sánchez, a senator for the National Action Party (PAN) from Tamaulipas, has confirmed her interest in running for mayor of Nuevo Laredo in the 2027 municipal elections, according to El Gráfico Tamaulipas.

Speaking with reporters, Sanmiguel said she has been in dialogue with both the national and state leadership of the PAN about the profiles that could represent the party in the upcoming elections, and that she will make herself available if the party considers her the right fit. “If the PAN so wishes, I will be there,” she said, as quoted by El Gráfico Tamaulipas.

Sanmiguel pointed to more than two decades of membership in Acción Nacional and to polling on her public image that, she said, registers no negative opinions. “Of course — any politician wants to govern their city. I have been in Nuevo Laredo my whole life, I have a love for Nuevo Laredo, and if the party wishes it and asks it of me, I would represent it,” she said, according to El Gráfico Tamaulipas.

The early numbers

Muro Político reported that Sanmiguel said internal party measurements place her at 22 percent in preferences among PAN aspirants for the Nuevo Laredo mayoral nomination. The outlet noted that she did not present details on sample size, methodology, or field dates for the surveys she cited.

An Electoralia poll published in October 2026, covered by Noticiero de Victoria, likewise placed Sanmiguel at 22 percent among PAN profiles for the nomination, with 41 percent of respondents saying they had not yet decided. In the same poll, Carlos de Anda led preferences on the Morena side with 29 percent. Noticiero de Victoria noted Sanmiguel’s local record: she has served as a Nuevo Laredo city council member, headed the municipal Secretariat of Public Works, Urban Development and Environment, and completed two terms as a local deputy before reaching the Senate.

Tamaulipas outlets have continued to feature Sanmiguel in their political coverage this month, including reports on a PAN gathering held October 16 covered by La Razón de Tamaulipas and Expreso. The PAN has not yet formally selected its candidate for Nuevo Laredo, and no official nomination has been announced.
